query: event sourcing state persistence architecture patterns
title: Microservices Pattern: Pattern: Event sourcing
snippet: Event sourcing persists the state of a business entity such as an Order or a Customer as a sequence of state-changing events. Whenever the state of a business entity changes, a new event is appended to the list of events.
claim: Event sourcing persists application state as an append-only sequence of immutable state-changing events.

query: durable state storage relational database vs event log
title: Relational vs event-native databases: how they compare
snippet: Relational databases store current state; when a row is updated or deleted, that data is thrown away, taking with it your data integrity and insight around what exactly happened. Event logs preserve all state transitions as immutable facts.
claim: Event logs preserve all state transitions as immutable facts, whereas relational databases discard historical update information.

query: object store state persistence distributed systems
title: Providing Persistent Objects in Distributed Systems
snippet: A persistent object store decouples the object model from individual programs, effectively providing a persistent heap that can be shared by many different programs: objects in the heap survive and can be used by applications so long as they can be referenced.
claim: Persistent object stores provide a shared persistent heap that enables objects to survive across program executions and be referenced by multiple applications.
